---
title: Keep a copy in sync with the event stream
sidebar_label: Keep a copy in sync
description: Follow an instance's event stream from a cursor, so a copy of your data stays current and picks up where it stopped after a break.
job: A builder follows the event stream from a cursor so their copy stays current and resumes after a break.
kind: tutorial
---

- **You'll build** a script that keeps a copy of an instance's files current and resumes after a break.
- **You need** Node.js 22.18 or later, a key that reads `core.file` and its subtypes ([Manage keys](/use/manage-keys)) in `MARFA_API_KEY`, and the instance's address in `MARFA_API_URL`.
- **You'll have** a `files-copy.json` that follows every change, whatever breaks.

A search index, a cache or a report keeps its own copy of an instance's data. Read it once, then apply each change from the [event stream](/build/events) and save a cursor, so a break loses nothing. Swift apps use a [working copy](/build/working-copies).

## What the stream sends

From cursor `21`, narrowed to files, `marfa events` prints one frame a line:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa events --type core.file --edges none --cursor 21
```

```text
-  stream_cursor  25
22  item.created  01a1f126-5ad1-7029-8f69-a66a15ee406d
23  item.trashed  01a1f124-12c1-7762-af28-52450dd463af
25  item.purged  01a1f124-12c1-7762-af28-52450dd463af
-  stream_live  25
```

</Terminal>

Over HTTP, [the stream](/reference/api/event-stream/streamEvents) takes your cursor in `Last-Event-ID` and answers server-sent events. It opens with `stream_cursor`, the **head of the log**, replays every event after your cursor, sends `stream_live` once caught up, then each new one. **The last `id:` you received is always a cursor you can resume from.**

## Build the sync

A browser `EventSource` can't send an `Authorization` header and the [TypeScript SDK](/reference/typescript-sdk) doesn't read streams, so read it with `fetch`, taking each frame as it arrives: Marfa closes a reader that takes nothing for 30 seconds. A refusal keeps its status and its `Retry-After`, which the loop at the end reads:

```ts title="sync.ts"
const baseUrl = process.env.MARFA_API_URL!;
const credential = process.env.MARFA_API_KEY!;

function refusal(what: string, response: Response) {
  const retryAfter = Number(response.headers.get("Retry-After")) || undefined;
  return Object.assign(new Error(`${what} answered ${response.status}`), { status: response.status, retryAfter });
}
```

`frames` yields each frame of the stream:

```ts title="sync.ts"
async function* frames(cursor?: string, signal?: AbortSignal) {
  const response = await fetch(`${baseUrl}/events?type=core.file&edges=none`, {
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${credential}`, ...(cursor && { "Last-Event-ID": cursor }) },
    signal,
  });
  if (!response.ok || !response.body) throw refusal("The stream", response);
  let buffer = "";
  for await (const text of response.body.pipeThrough(new TextDecoderStream())) {
    const blocks = (buffer + text).split("\n\n");
    buffer = blocks.pop() ?? "";
    for (const block of blocks) {
      const frame = { id: "", event: "message", data: "" };
      for (const line of block.split("\n")) {
        const [, field, value] = /^([^:]+):\s?(.*)$/.exec(line) ?? [];
        if (field === "id" || field === "event" || field === "data") frame[field] = value;
      }
      if (frame.data) yield frame;
    }
  }
}
```

**Save the cursor in the same place as the copy, in step with what you apply.** Every item event, and `metadata.changed`, carries the item as it stands after the change and its `metadata`, the tags and extensions the key may read. So `apply` replaces both together, or removes them for `item.purged`. `item.trashed` keeps the item, in the bin:

```ts title="sync.ts"
import { readFile, rename, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { createClient, pages, type components } from "@withmarfa/client";

const marfa = createClient({ baseUrl, credential });
type Entry = { item: components["schemas"]["Item"]; metadata: unknown };
let copy: { cursor?: string; files: Record<string, Entry> } =
  await readFile("files-copy.json", "utf8").then(JSON.parse, () => ({ files: {} }));

function apply(files: typeof copy.files, event: { event_type: string } & Entry) {
  if (event.event_type === "item.purged") delete files[event.item.id];
  else files[event.item.id] = { item: event.item, metadata: event.metadata };
}

async function saveCursor(cursor: string) {
  copy.cursor = cursor;
  await writeFile("files-copy.tmp", JSON.stringify(copy));
  await rename("files-copy.tmp", "files-copy.json"); // a crash never leaves half a file
}
```

`follow` applies each event, saves its ID, and returns the frame that ended the stream. It saves the `cursor` of `stream_live` too: on a narrow stream the last event can be far behind the head. When its `signal` ends the stream on purpose, it returns `reconcile`:

```ts title="sync.ts"
async function follow(cursor: string, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<string> {
  try {
    for await (const frame of frames(cursor, signal)) {
      const data = JSON.parse(frame.data);
      if (frame.event === "stream_cursor") continue;
      if (frame.event === "stream_live") await saveCursor(data.cursor);
      else if (["stream_incomplete", "catchup_too_old", "cursor_ahead"].includes(frame.event)) return frame.event;
      else {
        apply(copy.files, data);
        await saveCursor(frame.id);
      }
    }
  } catch (error) {
    if (!signal.aborted) throw error;
    return "reconcile";
  }
  return "closed";
}
```

`rebuild` takes the head of the log from the first frame and **refuses to go on without it**: with no cursor to resume from, a new stream sends only what is written from then on, and the changes between would be lost. It lists every file in every state with its metadata into a new copy, then saves the head as the cursor, so changes made meanwhile wait in the log. A failed listing leaves the old copy as it was:

```ts title="sync.ts"
async function rebuild(): Promise<string> {
  let head = "";
  for await (const frame of frames()) {
    if (frame.event === "stream_cursor") head = JSON.parse(frame.data).cursor;
    break; // the first frame names the head, and breaking closes the stream
  }
  if (!head) throw new Error("The stream didn't name the head of the log");
  const files: typeof copy.files = {};
  const listing = pages(async (cursor) => {
    const { data, error, response } = await marfa.GET("/items", {
      params: { query: { type: "core.file", state: "any", include: "metadata", cursor } },
    });
    if (error) throw refusal("The listing", response);
    return data;
  });
  for await (const row of listing) apply(files, { event_type: "item.created", ...(row as Entry) });
  copy = { files };
  await saveCursor(head);
  return head;
}
```

The loop resumes from the saved cursor after a break and rebuilds when the cursor can't be used. A refusal that a retry can't change stops it; `429` waits as long as `Retry-After` says, and a network fault waits five seconds. Once a day it ends the stream and rebuilds, because **a file retyped out of `core.file` is never announced on this stream**, and a key that reads only files wouldn't hear of it on any. The rebuild drops it:

```ts title="sync.ts"
const reconcileEvery = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
let cursor = copy.cursor;
for (;;) {
  let wait = 1000;
  try {
    cursor ??= await rebuild();
    const ended = await follow(cursor, AbortSignal.timeout(reconcileEvery));
    cursor = ["catchup_too_old", "cursor_ahead", "reconcile"].includes(ended) ? undefined : copy.cursor;
  } catch (error) {
    const { status = 0, retryAfter } = error as { status?: number; retryAfter?: number };
    if (status >= 400 && status < 500 && status !== 429) throw error; // a fault in the key or request
    wait = retryAfter ? retryAfter * 1000 : 5000;
    cursor = copy.cursor; // resume from what the copy holds; none rebuilds
    console.error(`${error}; trying again in ${wait / 1000}s`);
  }
  await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, wait));
}
```

Run it as a module and add a file with `marfa items add`: the copy follows. Stop the server and start it again: the loop reports the fault, waits and resumes from the saved cursor.

## When the stream ends

| You see | It means | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The connection closes with no frame | A network fault, or your reader took nothing for 30 seconds. | Resume from your saved cursor. |
| `stream_incomplete` | The stream couldn't go on, for its `reason`. | Resume from your cursor; for `credential_ended`, with a valid key. |
| `catchup_too_old` | The log no longer holds the events after your cursor (30 days by default). | Rebuild from the head of the log. |
| `cursor_ahead` | Your cursor is past the head, as after a restore from a backup. | Discard the cursor and rebuild. |

A refusal before the stream opens is a fault in the key or request, except `429 rate_limited`, which names the seconds to wait in `Retry-After`, and `503 stream_capacity_exhausted`, which asks you to try later.

## Narrow the stream, or catch up by listing

`type` takes up to ten types or patterns, each with its subtypes, and a cursor works under any filter. Edge events come whatever `type` says, so `sync.ts` sends `edges=none`.

To catch up without the stream, [list items](/reference/api/items/listItems) with `updated_after`, or `--updated-after` in the CLI, set to the latest `updated_at` you hold. **Add `state=any`** (`--state any`), since a listing answers only active items, and `include=metadata`. The bound includes items changed at that instant, so **replace each item you hold by its `id`**: two changes to one item can share an instant, and skipping it would lose the second. A listing can't report a purged item, or one retyped out of your types; the stream can report a purge.

The rules are in the [events](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/events.md) chapter of the contract.
